paragraphs: Friend, here's what this chapter is really about: when God's house gets built, nothing gets rushed and nothing gets skimped. Solomon spent seven years on the house of the LORD and thirteen on his own palace (1 Kings 6:38; 7:1). I think the point isn't to compare the two. It's that the work on the LORD's house is carried through to the very end, right down to the gold hinges on the doors (1 Kings 7:50). So when you're tempted to cut a corner on the things of God, remember that this story took its time.

Now look at who does the work. Huram is brought from Tyre, and the text says he had "great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work" (1 Kings 7:14). He comes to King Solomon and carries out all his work (1 Kings 7:14). God's house gets built by people who bring what they know how to do. You don't have to be the king. You just have to show up and do your part with all you've got, and Huram did that, and the work got finished (1 Kings 7:40).

And don't miss the last part, because it hits me right in the apron. There was so much bronze that Solomon left it "unweighed" (1 Kings 7:47), and then he brought in the silver, gold and furnishings his father David had dedicated (1 Kings 7:51). Some of the work was done by Solomon, and some was given years before by David, and all of it went into the house of the LORD. Your faithful work matters in a bigger story than you can see. Keep your oven warm, friend, because this story is not over.
